title: Deloading Practices in Strength and Physique Sports: A Cross-sectional Survey
population: 246 competitive strength and physique athletes (181 men, 65 women; mean age 29.5; about 8 years of training).
key_findings: All athletes reported deloading, mainly to manage energy and fatigue.
A typical deload lasted about 6.4 days and came about every 5.6 weeks, mostly pre-planned, sometimes combined with an autoregulated trigger such as stalled performance, soreness or joint aches.
Athletes reported cutting volume, load and effort (more repetitions in reserve) while keeping frequency and exercise selection.
methods: Anonymous 55-item web survey of a convenience sample.
limitations: Self-reported practice from a convenience sample; it describes what athletes do, not whether deloading works.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
